title: Ames: original righteousness a moral condition owed to a nature made to act justly
source_text: XXVIII. Amesius in Bellarmino Enervato tomo quarto capite primo, explicans quomodo justitia Originalis primo homini naturalis fuerit, Nos non dicimus, inquit, justitiam illam fuisse vel essentialem partem naturae Physicae, aut Physico modo ex ejus principiis fluere, sed conditionem esse moralem naturae illi debitam, quae ad juste operandum fuit creata.
pass_a_gloss: Ames in Bellarmine Enervated volume four chapter one, explaining how Original justice was natural to the first man, We do not say, he says, that that justice was either an essential part of Physical nature, or flowed in a Physical way from its principles, but that it was a moral condition owed to that nature, which was created for acting justly.
pass_b_english: William Ames, in volume 4, chapter 1 of his Bellarmine Disarmed, explains how original righteousness was natural to the first man: "We do not say that this righteousness was an essential part of physical nature or flowed from its principles in a physical way. We say it was a moral condition owed to that nature, which was created to act righteously."

choices.why: Ames contrasts physical (natural-causal) and moral; both words are kept.
